8: # fetching-salesforce-docs
9: 
10: Use this skill to retrieve and ground answers in **official Salesforce documentation on the public web**.
11: 
12: This skill provides a **reliable online retrieval playbook** for Salesforce docs that are hard to fetch, especially `help.salesforce.com`, JS-heavy `developer.salesforce.com`, Lightning Design System docs on `lightningdesignsystem.com`, and other official Salesforce-owned doc pages such as `architect.salesforce.com` and `admin.salesforce.com`.
13: 
14: Optional extraction scripts are available in `scripts/` — see the Reference File Index below.
15: 
16: ## Scope
17: 
18: | | |
19: |---|---|
20: | **In scope** | Official Salesforce doc retrieval: Apex, API, LWC, metadata, Agentforce, setup articles, SLDS, architect/admin guidance |
21: | **Out of scope** | Third-party blogs, PDF fallback, local corpus indexing, benchmark workflows, generating code or metadata |
22: 
23: ## Required Inputs
24: 
25: Before fetching, identify:
26: - The exact concept, identifier, class, method, or feature name being requested
27: - The likely doc family (developer docs, help articles, design system, architect/admin)
28: 
29: No additional setup is required to use the retrieval playbook in this skill. The optional extraction scripts require `playwright` — see `requirements.txt`.
30: 
31: ## Official Sources Only
32: 
33: Prefer Salesforce-owned documentation sources:
34: - `developer.salesforce.com`
35: - `help.salesforce.com`
36: - `architect.salesforce.com`
37: - `admin.salesforce.com`
38: - `lightningdesignsystem.com`
39: - other official Salesforce documentation pages when Salesforce uses them as the source of truth
40: 
41: Avoid third-party blogs, videos, or summary articles unless the user explicitly asks for them.
42: 
43: Do **not** fall back to PDFs.
44: 
45: ## Retrieval Workflow
46: 
47: ### 1. Classify the request first
48: 
49: Before fetching anything, identify the likely doc family.
50: 
51: | Family | Typical Source | Use For |
52: |---|---|---|
53: | Developer docs | `developer.salesforce.com/docs/...` | Apex, APIs, LWC, metadata, Agentforce developer docs |
54: | Help docs | `help.salesforce.com/...` | setup, admin, product configuration |
55: | Architect/Admin docs | `architect.salesforce.com/...`, `admin.salesforce.com/...` | best practices, patterns, well-architected guidance, admin enablement |
56: | Design system docs | `lightningdesignsystem.com/...` | SLDS, Cosmos, design tokens, component and styling guidance |
57: | Legacy atlas docs | `developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.*` | older official guide and reference docs |
58: 
59: ### 2. Identify the exact concept
60: 
61: Extract the real target before you search:
62: - exact API/class/method name
63: - exact feature name
64: - exact product phrase
65: - exact setup concept
66: 
67: Examples:
68: - `Lightning Message Service`
69: - `Wire Service`
70: - `System.StubProvider`
71: - `Agentforce Actions`
72: - `Messaging for In-App and Web allowed domains`
73: 
74: ### 3. Prefer targeted official retrieval
75: 
76: Do **not** broad-crawl Salesforce docs.
77: 
78: Instead:
79: 1. identify the most likely official guide root or article
80: 2. if search is needed, restrict it to official Salesforce domains only
81: 3. fetch that official page
82: 4. check whether the **exact concept actually appears on the page**
83: 5. if not, inspect and follow the most relevant **1–3 official child links**
84: 6. stop once you have grounded evidence
85: 
86: ### 4. Do not stop at broad landing pages
87: 
88: A guide landing page is **not enough** unless it clearly contains the exact requested concept.
89: 
90: This is especially important for:
91: - LWC docs
92: - Agentforce docs
93: - broad platform guide homepages
94: - help landing pages that link to the real article
95: 
96: ### 5. For `developer.salesforce.com`
97: 
98: Use this playbook:
99: - start with the most likely official guide root
100: - if the page is JS-heavy, prefer browser-rendered extraction
101: - check whether the exact concept appears on the page
102: - if the concept is missing, inspect official child links and follow the best matching 1–3 links
103: - prefer exact concept pages over broad guide roots
104: - legacy atlas pages are valid if they are the real official reference for the concept
105: 
106: ### 6. For `help.salesforce.com`
107: 
108: Help pages often fail with naive fetching.
109: 
110: Use this playbook:
111: - prefer exact `articleView?id=...` URLs when available
112: - use browser-rendered extraction when plain fetch returns shell content
113: - treat outputs like `Loading`, `Sorry to interrupt`, `CSS Error`, or mostly chrome/navigation text as **failed extraction**, not evidence
114: - look for the **real article body**, not just header, nav, or footer text
115: - reject shell pages and soft-404 pages such as:
116:   - "We looked high and low but couldn't find that page"
117:   - generic empty help shells
118: - if starting from a nearby guide or hub page, follow linked Help articles until you reach the real article body
119: - if extraction still fails after targeted retries, return the best official Help URLs you found and explicitly say that article-body extraction was unsuccessful
120: 
121: ## Acceptance Rules
122: 
123: A page is good enough to answer from only when at least one of these is true:
124: - the exact identifier appears on the page
125: - the exact concept phrase appears on the page
126: - multiple query-specific phrases appear in the correct official context
127: 
128: A page is **not** good enough when:
129: - it is only a broad landing page
130: - it is a shell page with little real article text
131: - it is from the wrong product area
132: - it does not contain the requested identifier or concept
133: - it is a third-party explanation when an official page should exist
134: 
135: ## Rejection Rules
136: 
137: Reject these as final evidence:
138: - broad guide homepages without the exact concept
139: - release notes when a concept/reference page is expected
140: - admin blog posts when developer docs are requested
141: - third-party blogs when official docs are available
142: - shell-rendered pages with no real article body
143: - pages whose titles sound right but whose body does not contain the requested concept
144: 
145: ## Grounding Requirements
146: 
147: When answering, include:
148: 1. guide/article title
149: 2. exact official URL
150: 3. source type:
151:    - developer doc page
152:    - atlas reference page
153:    - help article page
154: 4. any caveat if extraction was partial or browser-rendered
155: 
156: If evidence is weak, say so plainly.
157: 
158: ## Examples
159: 
160: ### Example: Lightning Message Service
161: Do **not** stop at the general LWC guide root.
162: Find the exact LWC page for Lightning Message Service or follow the most relevant child links from the LWC docs until the exact concept appears.
163: 
164: ### Example: Wire Service
165: Do **not** answer from the LWC homepage unless `Wire Service` is actually present there.
166: Follow the relevant child doc page for wire service or wire adapters.
167: 
168: ### Example: Agentforce Actions
169: Do **not** answer from a broad Agentforce landing page or a blog post.
170: Find the official Agentforce developer page for actions, or follow the best matching child pages from the official Agentforce docs.
171: 
172: ### Example: Messaging for In-App and Web allowed domains
173: Prefer official Help articles and browser-rendered extraction.
174: Reject generic help shells. Follow linked Help articles from nearby official messaging docs if needed.
175: 
176: ### Example: System.StubProvider
177: Prefer the official Salesforce reference/developer page where the exact identifier appears.
178: Do not substitute a broader Apex landing page if the identifier is absent.
179: 
180: ## Non-Goals
181: 
182: This skill should **not**:
183: - maintain a local documentation corpus
184: - rely on a local index
185: - use PDF fallback
186: - run benchmark workflows
187: - depend on repo-specific scripts to be useful
188: 
189: ## Output Expectations
190: 
191: For each retrieval, include:
192: 1. Guide or article title
193: 2. Exact official URL
194: 3. Source type (developer doc page / atlas reference page / help article page)
195: 4. Any caveat if extraction was partial or browser-rendered
196: 
197: If evidence is weak, say so plainly rather than forcing an answer.

15: - traverses nested shadow roots
16: - prioritizes Salesforce Help article-body containers such as `.slds-text-longform`
17: - returns structured JSON with the extracted article text and official child links
